Mỗi 110 px = 100 lần. RAM nhanh hơn RTT: Every 110 px = 100×. RAM is roughly 1.5 million times faster than an intercontinental RTT.
Phân phối latency thực tế luôn lệch phải: Real latency distributions are always right-skewed
Trung bình nằm bên phải p50 và vẫn thấp: The mean sits right of p50 and is still almost 4× below p95: it describes nobody.

Thang logarit so sánh bậc độ lớn của các: A log scale comparing the orders of magnitude of different kinds of latency
Thang logarit: mỗi bước 110 px tương ứng: A log scale: each 110 px step is 100×. It is precisely because this scale is logarithmic that our linear intuition keeps failing.
Histogram latency lệch phải với các vạch: A right-skewed latency histogram with markers at p50, the mean, p95 and p99
Hình dạng này là mặc định của hệ thống t: This shape is the default for real systems, not a pathological case. The right tail comes from GC pauses, cache misses, lock contention, retries and queueing.
Đồ thị mức chiếm dụng rho với thời gian: A plot of utilisation rho against waiting time, with a vertical asymptote at rho = 1
Vùng xanh (ρ &lt; 0,6) là nơi trực giác:
The green zone (ρ < 0.6) is where linear intuition still holds. From the amber zone onwards, every extra percent of load is paid for with several percent of latency.
The markers on this chart are time waiting in the queue relative to service time, that is $\rho/(1-\rho)$ — not the total time in the system $W$. The two differ by exactly 1: at $\rho = 0.7$, queueing time is 2.3 times the service time, while total time in the system is 3.3 times what it is when idle.
